articles.title: China’s Space Epoch raises new funding, targets 2026 launch and recovery attempt
articles.summary:
Chinese launch startup Space Epoch has secured B-round funding as the company moves towards a first orbital launch and recovery attempt late this year.
The post China’s Space Epoch raises new funding, targets 2026 launch and recovery attempt appeared first on SpaceNews.

articles.title: Stormy, Snowy Winter for Hokkaido
articles.summary: On February 5, 2026, the MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) on NASA’s Terra satellite acquired this image of snow-covered landscapes across Hokkaido. With more than 31 active volcanoes, the island features several large caldera lakes, including at least five that are visible in the image. articles.title: NASA Advances High-Altitude Traffic Management
articles.summary: High-altitude flight is getting increasing attention from sectors ranging from telecommunications to emergency response. To make that airspace more accessible, NASA is developing an air traffic management system covering those altitudes and supplementing its work with real-time data from a research balloon in Earth’s stratosphere.  Aircraft at high altitudes – 50,000 feet or higher, or roughly 10,000 to 20,000 feet above most commercial traffic – offer new […]

articles.title: SatVu to expand thermal imaging constellation with NATO-backed funds
articles.summary:
Earth observation startup SatVu said Feb. 17 it has raised $41 million in a funding round that included the NATO Innovation Fund, as commercial space-based thermal imagery gains traction with defense and intelligence agencies.
The post SatVu to expand thermal imaging constellation with NATO-backed funds appeared first on SpaceNews.

articles.title: NASA Tests SLS Umbilicals, Prepares for Second Wet Dress Rehearsal
articles.summary: Following the incomplete first Wet Dress Rehearsal for the Artemis II mission earlier this month due to hydrogen leaks, the Exploration Ground Systems team decided that more testing was needed.
